## Definitions: Simple Random and Systematic Sampling

::: {.callout title="Definitions"}
A **simple random sample** is a sample selected in such a way that every element of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.

A **systematic sample** is a sample in which every $K^{th}$ element in the sampling frame (the list of population elements) is selected after a suitable random start for the first element.
:::

## Example: Simple Random Sample

An analyst has a database containing 10,000 short-form videos. They assign each video a unique number from 1 to 10,000 and use a random number generator to select 346 of those numbers. Every video in the database has the same chance of being selected.

This is a **simple random sample**.

## Example: Systematic Sample

A platform provides an analyst with a list of videos in chronological order. The analyst randomly chooses one of the first 29 videos as a starting point, then selects every 29th video after that until 346 videos have been selected.

This is a **systematic sample**. The random start helps avoid a predictable pattern in the selection.

## Practice: Every Tenth Video

A research assistant watches a live feed of newly posted videos. They randomly choose one of the first 10 videos, then select every 10th video after that for review.

What type of sampling method is this?

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout title="Solution"}
This is a **systematic sample**. After a random start, the assistant selects every $K^{th}$ video, where $K = 10$.
:::
:::

## Definitions: Stratified, Cluster, and Multistage Sampling

::: {.callout title="Definitions"}
A **stratified sample** is obtained by dividing the population into nonoverlapping groups called strata, then randomly selecting a proportional number of elements from each stratum.

In **cluster sampling**, the sampling unit is a group of elements called a cluster. Clusters are usually natural groups, and entire selected clusters are included in the sample.

**Multistage sampling** collects information from the whole sample and then collects additional data, either at the same time or later, from subsamples.
:::

## Example: Stratified Sample

An analyst wants to ensure that each platform is represented in the sample. They divide all videos into three strata: YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram Reels. Then they randomly select videos from each stratum in proportion to its size in the population, roughly 41% YouTube, 36% TikTok, and 23% Instagram Reels.

This is a **stratified sample**.

## Example: Cluster Sample

An analyst randomly selects 20 creators from a large list of creators and then includes **every video** posted by those 20 creators in the sample.

This is a **cluster sample**. The creators are the clusters, and all videos within each selected cluster are included.

## Practice: Platforms, Creators, and Videos

A national study selects 2 platforms at random. Within each selected platform, the researchers randomly choose 15 creators. Finally, they randomly select 5 videos from each selected creator.

What type of sampling method is this?

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout title="Solution"}
This is **multistage sampling**. The researchers sample in stages: platforms, then creators within platforms, then videos within creators.
:::
:::
